entry.note: Successor check of this claim under the frozen Spec 064 contract (OSF s6hr9, approved + public), successor to Spec 046's first check, which stands unedited in this record under 'first_check'. Step 0 passed in full, including gate 0.4: the preserved drawn-form reference at its pinned digest (33ee22ec…) and the thesis file's digest asserted on the local file before any plate was read. Step 1 named the source's sign list from the book's own apparatus (Wells's own list, Wells 2011, in Wells 2015 Chapter 2 / Figure 2.6); step D derived the drawn-form descriptor twice, independently, from the thesis plate (Figure 3.2, thesis p. 90 / PDF p. 102) and sustained the preserved reference; step C — mandatory in Spec 064 — was not sustained: neither independent derivation affirms that the descriptor picks out plate 297 and no neighbour in the 289–308 run (signs 299, 302 and 303 satisfy every stated feature of the descriptor), so the run closed as IDENTIFICATION FAILED (continuity/discrimination not sustained) before step M and before any scoring. The preserved reference's continuity status is QUALIFIED — anchored at family level only — and is carried on every product of the run. This is a check of identification, recorded under F064-C15: it is not a verdict on the identification, and the claim's status and stage are unchanged. Appended by the Spec 064 execution; no pre-existing field of any claim in this file was altered, and the Spec 046 first_check entry is unedited.
entry.wording: The fragment 'sign 297 is the horned tiger' cannot be carried to a concordance: the descriptor's discrimination of 297 from its neighbours in the 289–308 run was not sustained by both independent derivations. The record stays a stated gap. No statement about the sign is made, and nothing is fed to Asset A. Qualification (carried from the preserved reference, Spec 064 §1): the identification of Wells's 297 rests on a drawn-form reference whose continuity status is QUALIFIED — anchored at family level only; its step C discrimination check is part of this run's record.

gate_0_2.passage_quote: Sign 532 and sign 297 are positioned in such a way as to resemble the position of the graphic element and several of their features are repeated in the image field. It is proposed here that sign 532 is a logograph for the anthropomorphic figure and that sign 297 represents the horned tiger, or perhaps just ‘tiger’ generically.

step_c.family_anchor_carried: Registry row P205 ('Prismed light rays, with opposite slanting on top vs bottom, more rays on bottom'), whose wells_ids cell groups W289-W306 as one Parpola sign's Wells counterparts — carried at its frozen status: corroboration only, expressly NOT an identification. step_c.statement: Step C is not sustained. Neither independent derivation affirms that the reconciled descriptor picks out the plate's 297 and no neighbour in the 289-308 run: signs 299, 302 and 303 satisfy every stated feature of the descriptor, and the remaining near neighbours differ only in degree on features the descriptor does not quantify. The family anchor is family-level only, exactly as the preserved reference records it. The run therefore closes under the pre-registered closure, before step M and before any scoring. The preserved reference's continuity status remains QUALIFIED.

noted_readings: stroke number: the preserved descriptor's 'four' is the count at the base; three strokes are clear above the bend, where the innermost strokes merge in the scan

lower direction: the preserved descriptor's 'near-vertical' reads on the plate as slanting down to the right at about 30 degrees from vertical — more vertical than the upper portions, not strictly vertical
comparison_with_preserved.reasoning: Both derivations confirm the preserved descriptor's feature set — a parallel bent bundle, a single bend, a steep upper slant down-left, a basal splay, in the bent-ray run. The two noted readings loosen the descriptor's wording without changing any feature it asserts, and the preserved record itself carries discrimination, not description, as the open step (its recorded limitation). No material difference arises, so the run does not close as IDENTIFICATION FAILED (reference not sustained); it proceeds to step C, where the discrimination is tested.
comparison_with_preserved.verdict: AGREEMENT — the preserved reference is sustained

features_read_for_297: a bundle of long parallel strokes
bent once, at a single bend whose point is at the left
the upper portions slant steeply down to the left
the lower portions run down from the bend and splay slightly apart at the base
stroke count read as four at the base, three clear above the bend
derivations.method: First plate read: full-page render of PDF p. 102 at 300 dpi, read in page context against the whole Figure 3.2 plate.
derivations.neighbour_set_discriminated_against: the plates' bent-ray run, signs 289-308: the upper row (289-294) are compact chevron forms with no long lower run; in the bottom row, 295 carries a single broad upper stroke, 296 and 304 keep their upper portions near-vertical, and 307 and 308 carry a looped head; 299, 300, 301, 302, 303, 305 and 306 are the same bent bundle in differing widths and counts.
derivations.plate_locator: Wells 2006, PhD thesis, Figure 3.2, 'The Indus signs by sign number', thesis p. 90 / PDF p. 102; bottom row, signs 295-308; 297 is the third entry.
derivations.step_c_statement: I cannot affirm that the descriptor picks out plate 297 and no neighbour. Signs 299, 302 and 303 present the same feature set — a parallel bundle bent once, uppers slanting steeply down-left, lowers running down from the bend with a basal splay — and nothing in the features I read separates 297 from them. What fixes 297 on the plate is its printed position and number, which is the number-only reading the protocol names as a trap when it is used without this check.

features_read_for_297: three distinct strokes above the bend
four distinct stroke ends at the base
a single sharp bend, point at the left, at about 55-60% of the glyph height
upper portions slant about 50 degrees from vertical, down to the left
lower portions slant about 30 degrees from vertical, down to the right — more vertical than the uppers, not strictly near-vertical
derivations.method: Second plate read: independent re-render of PDF p. 102; per-sign cell crops at 600-700 dpi; stroke counts taken at the top edge and at the base of each glyph in the 289-308 run.

derivations.plate_locator: Wells 2006, PhD thesis, Figure 3.2, thesis p. 90 / PDF p. 102; bottom row, signs 295-308; 297 is the third entry.
derivations.step_c_statement: I cannot affirm the discrimination. Counted feature by feature, signs 299, 302 and 303 match 297 on every feature the descriptor states (parallel bundle, single bend, steep upper slant, lower run with basal splay, four stroke ends at the base); 300, 301, 305 and 306 differ only in degree (width, bend sharpness, slant) on features the descriptor does not quantify. The descriptor fixes the family and 297's place in the run; it does not pick out 297 alone.

step_d.preserved_descriptor: Sign 297 is a bundle of four long parallel strokes bent once: the upper portions slant steeply down to the left; below the bend the strokes run near-vertical and splay slightly apart at the base. It stands in the plates' bent-ray run (signs 289-308), whose members differ in stroke count, bend position, and basal splay.
step_d.reconciled_descriptor: A bundle of long parallel strokes bent once at a single sharp bend — three strokes clear above the bend and four stroke ends at the base: the upper portions slant steeply down to the left; below the bend the strokes run down to the right, more vertical than the uppers, splaying at the base. A member of the thesis plates' bent-ray run (signs 289-308).
